title: Taylor Swift, Inducted Into Nashville Songwriters Hall of Fame, Says ‘There Is No Music Community Like This Music Community. I Know, I Checked All the Communities’
description: Taylor Swift looked back on her earliest days crafting songs in Music City as she was inducted Monday  into the Nashville Songwriters Hall of Fame,
body:
Taylor Swift looked back on her earliest days crafting songs in Music City as she was inducted Monday  into the Nashville Songwriters Hall of Fame, becoming its youngest member at 36. Swift was inducted by former tourmate Brad Paisley, whom she teased, and serenaded by Lainey Wilson, whom she praised, before launching into a lengthy speech about what she learned in the trenches of Music Row as a teenager.

	“I was lucky enough to get a publishing deal with Sony Publishing when I was 14, and I just hit the ground running,” she told the audience at the Music City Center ceremony. “I was like a sponge, and I have really curly hair and it was yellow, so I kind of looked like a sponge too,” she quipped.
	

	Praising the town that she said raised her, Swift said, per Rolling Stone, “There is no music community like this music community. I know. I checked all the communities.” 



	

					(L-R) Lyle Lovett, Shawn Camp, Lee Thomas Miller, Taylor Swift, George Strait and Bruce Channel attend the 56th Nashville Songwriters Hall Of Fame Gala at Music City Center on October 26, 2026 in Nashville, Tennessee. (Photo by Kevin Mazur/Getty Images for TAS)
									Ed Rode
	



	Swift was being inducted alongside Lyle Lovett, Bruce Channel, Shawn Camp and Lee Thomas Miller (plus the late J.I. Allison, of Buddy Holly and the Crickets). Also being honored with a special award at the ceremony was country superstar George Strait, who was getting the Career Maker Award, something only one other artist has received, in honor of what he has accomplished for others performing their material.

	The tradition at Nashville Songwriters Hall of Fame ceremonies is for the inductees not to sing or play themselves but rather to enjoy a performance of one of their songs by another notable star or major figure. In this case it was Lainey Wilson doing a stripped-back version of “Love Story,” to which Swift offered some reciprocal support by getting in a plug for Wilson’s new single.
	


	“You know, I first of all want to say thank you to Lainey Wilson, who I just think is one of the coolest people in the world,” Swift said, “for saying yes and doing that. And I’ve had her new single on repeat. It just puts me in the best mood. It’s called ‘Kinda Love It.’ Check it out.”

	Paisley gave an introduction in which he recalled marveling at how she went from proving she was a star with her first two albums and proving once and for all that she was a songwriting all-timer with her entirely self-penned third album. “All of us were like, ‘How is this teenager doing this? How is she so brilliant?’ And then she goes off and really put her feelings into something that is 100% hers and writes the ‘Speak Now’ album all by herself,” he reminisced. “It’s an amazing thing to watch her evolution from somebody who realized this all starts with a song to (being able to) take that exact thing and change the world with it.”

	In turn, Swift turned the laudatory mood more light-hearted as she recalled the days when she opened for Paisley on a summer amphitheater tour between her first and second albums. He and his band and his opening acts would always famously play prans on each other, and Swift suggested it might have gone a bit too next-level by the end.

	“Brad Paisley, thank you so much for that induction. I’m really surprised to see you here, actually,” she said, “because we’ve been estranged since 2007. I think you know why. Crickets. He took a tour prank too far. Filled my entire tour bus with live crickets. Thousands of them. Oh my God. For months, I couldn’t sleep. Just chirp… chirp… chirp.” A pause, and then, again: “Chirp — all night. I considered buying a pet lizard to eradicate the problem. It was a dark time. But you know what? You did such an amazing job with that introduction, I think we can let bygones be bygones. Thank you. Yeah, I think we’re good now.”

	Getting into the serious grist of her speech, Swift focused on the three words that make up the primary name of her honor — “Nashville,” “Songwriters” and “Fame” — and devoted individual time to each of them.

	She said that even as a young child, songwriting was “what I centered my entire life around,” and Nashville became “the place that I went to in my middle school daydreams. It was the place where all the wisdom that I wished to acquire existed in one place. … And it ended up being all of that and more. It ended up being everything.”
	



	

					Taylor Swift attends the 56th Nashville Songwriters Hall Of Fame Gala at Music City Center on October 26, 2026 in Nashville, Tennessee.  (Photo by Kevin Mazur/Getty Images for TAS)
									Kevin Mazur/Getty Images for TAS
	



	As for the fame part, Swift described that as almost incidental, yet also almost all-consuming, as “a byproduct of my love for music. … It’s why a lot of people know the words to my music, which is awesome. It’s also why there’s these daily random doses of chaos that just pop up in my life every once in a while — every couple of hours. That can be weird, but I have tools in place in my mind that help me navigate that and get back to true north when life feels so bizarre. Those tools are my memories,” and she suggested that “the memories that I visit most frequently when I need to return back to some semblance of remembering what normalcy is and why I do this” are from her early years in Nashville.

	Swift credited songwriting sessions as a kid as places where she “learned which ideas are worth fighting for (and) which ideas are worth letting go of… I learned how to accommodate when your co-writer has a hangover, or when they’re going to need to talk about their divorce for a really long time before we write anything. One thing that I did learn is that songwriters, although they possess the superhuman ability to understand and interpret the human condition and have insane levels of empathy — they re just people too. And they are people who in a lot of ways raised me and guided me through my formative years.”




	Swift did a bit of name-dropping, like how she got to know not just Catherine, the woman who worked the front desk at the Jody Williams Music publishing company, but her boyfriend and future husband, Eric Church. She mentioned running up the stairs to the writing room to meet up with frequent collaborator Liz Rose, where she would say, “Liz, this happened at school today…” And then she would run to the garden shed behind the building that was the one-person studio for Nathan Chapman, who played every instrument on her demos and “interpreted my music so intuitively that later on I would fight for him to produce my entire first album. It was our first album, for both of us. And I am shocked and stunned to say that as of a couple days ago, that album is 20 years old.”
	

	In summary, Swift said, “It’s not lost on me how crazy this is. I will cherish it forever because Nashville is the place that honed and polished the thing about myself and the thing about my life that I am the most proud of and the most passionate about… It just feels like one of those amazing Nashville moments I’m going to revisit on a rainy day.”

	Swift, who was wearing a burgundy floral Raina Vanessa minidress to the ceremony, was getting the honor just four months after she received a similar accolade. She was inducted into the Songwriters Hall of Fame in New York in June; she was also the youngest writer to receive that honor.

schema.headline: Taylor Swift, Inducted Into Nashville Songwriters Hall of Fame, Says ‘There Is No Music Community Like This Music Community. I Know, I Checked All the Communities’

title: Netflix Hires Steve Wilson to Lead Podcast Content Acquisition
description:
Netflix has hired Steve Wilson to head its podcast expansion, Variety has confirmed. 

	Wilson will lead the company’s podcast content acquisitions
body:
Netflix has hired Steve Wilson to head its podcast expansion, Variety has confirmed. 

	Wilson will lead the company’s podcast content acquisitions on a contract basis. Before heading to Netflix, Wilson spent 15 years at Apple, where he most recently headed marketing for Apple Podcasts and partnered with podcasters and networks. He left Apple in December 2020, and spent nearly six years at podcast studio QCode as chief strategy officer before joining Daylight Media in the same position.
	

	As reported in September, Netflix now offers more than 60 video podcasts on its service, and has continued to lean into expanding its catalog. The streamer’s original lineup of video podcasts currently includes true-crime show “Murder With My Husband”; talk show “The Pete Davidson Show” hosted by the “Saturday Night Live” alum; pop-culture interview show “Shut Up Evan” hosted by Evan Ross Katz; “The Puzzle Room With David Kwong”; and “Allegedly,” a true-crime podcast from NBC News correspondent Ellison Barber.

	Wilson joins Netflix at a tumultuous time, two weeks after the company announced layoffs of 6% of employees, equating to about 1,000 jobs. The cut was the biggest to date, and primarily affected workers in Netflix’s product, technology, legal and HR teams, according to an email to employees written by co-CEOs Ted Sarandos and Greg Peters.

	“Our mission — to entertain the world — is ambitious, and delivering on it requires us to be disciplined about where we prioritize our people and resources,” the co-CEOs said in the memo, a copy of which was obtained by Variety.
	

	Amid the layoffs, Netflix also ousted a number of chief executives, including chief content officer Bela Bajaria, head of film Dan Lin and his top lieutenant, Doug Belgrad, as well as director of original series Carolina Garcia. Veteran TV exec Peter Rice was tapped to replace Bajaria.

	When asked about the leadership change on the content side during the streamer’s Q3 2026 earnings call, co-CEO Ted Sarandos said, “I know that we could do better, and we want to build on that momentum.”

schema.headline: Netflix Hires Steve Wilson to Lead Podcast Content Acquisition

title: Disney+ Strikes Landmark Content Deal With U.K.’s Channel 4 That Streamer Says Is Among Its ‘Most Significant’ Globally
description: Disney+ has made what it claims is one of the “most significant’ content arrangements with broadcasters around the world to bring local content to
body:
Disney+ has made what it claims is one of the “most significant’ content arrangements with broadcasters around the world to bring local content to its platform, striking a landmark deal with U.K. network Channel 4. 

	The first-of-its-kind deal will see the Channel 4 service launch on Disney+ in the U.K. and Ireland in early 2027, with multiple Channel 4 shows made available on-demand each year on Disney+ at the same time as their release via Channel 4.  These shows include the drama “Maya” featuring Bella Ramsey, comedy “Stepping Up” featuring Denise Welch and reality format “Celebrity SAS: Who Dares Wins,” alongside – Channel 4’s main TV channel and additional on-demand content.
	

	The deal is one of around ten similar content deals that Disney has signed with international broadcasters, since it broke new ground last year following a deal with Brit streamer ITVX to share select content. That groundbreaking deal came just weeks after Netflix unveiled a landmark agreement in France to give its subscribers access to TF1 channels via the streamer.

	News of the collaboration with Channel 4 was described as “one of the most significant that Disney+ has agreed globally to bring high-quality, local content to customers in markets around the world,” according to Disney, something it said would enhance “Channel 4’s reach” and bring “more choice to Disney+ customers.”

	As per the deal, Disney+ customers will be able to watch Channel 4’s linear HD channel, plus hundreds of hours of its scripted and unscripted content through its on-demand catalogue, for no additional cost. The on-demand offering will feature a range of Channel 4 shows available day and dat’ on Disney+ – with Disney+ customers gaining access to multiple new Channel 4 shows each year as part of their existing subscription. Channel 4 will be available via a Channel 4-branded section.
	

	“We’re thrilled to be working with Disney+ to give audiences even more ways to discover and enjoy Channel 4’s brilliant shows,” said Priya Dogra, Channel 4 chief executive. “Channel 4 is home to some of the UK and Ireland’s most talked about and trusted programming, and this new service will help those shows reach viewers in new places. This exciting step shows how collaboration between broadcasters and streamers can create more choice and value for audiences.”

	Added Adam Smith, chairman direct-to-consumer, Disney Entertainment: “Local broadcaster partnerships are very important as we build our content libraries and serve fans around the world. Channel 4 has created shows with strong appeal to audiences in the UK and Ireland, and we’re excited to bring some of those favorites to Disney+. This agreement is the latest example of our global strategy, pairing high-quality local programming and cultural relevance with a complementary audience and more personalized streaming experience on Disney+.”

schema.headline: Disney+ Strikes Landmark Content Deal With U.K.’s Channel 4 That Streamer Says Is Among Its ‘Most Significant’ Globally

title: Hubert de la Bouillerie, Editor on ‘Woodstock,’ ‘Witches of Eastwick,’ Dies at 75
description: Hubert de la Bouillerie, who edited films including George Miller’s “The Witches of Eastwick” and “Tango & Cash,” died Aug. 8 in Los Angeles. He wa
body:
Hubert de la Bouillerie, who edited films including George Miller’s “The Witches of Eastwick” and “Tango & Cash,” died Aug. 8 in Los Angeles. He was 75.

	Among his credits was additional editing on the 1970 documentary “Woodstock,” along with “Highlander II: The Quickening,” “Mo’ Money,” “Doin’ Time,” “Blank Check” and “Celtic Pride.”

	He also served as editor on “Police Academy 5” and “Police Academy 6.” 
	

	De la Bouillerie also moved behind the camera as a director. His directing credits included the 1996 television film “The Right to Remain Silent,” whose ensemble cast included Lea Thompson, LL Cool J, Patrick Dempsey, Christopher Lloyd, Amanda Plummer and Carl Reiner, as well as the 1997 science-fiction film “The Apocalypse.”

	His wife, Debbie Robins de la Bouillerie, pre-deceased him. Earlier in his life, Hubert was married to Hilary Saltzman, daughter of film producer Harry Saltzman, who, together with Albert R. Broccoli, brought the original James Bond film series to the screen.

	Later in his career, Hubert continued to develop his own projects as a writer and producer, reflecting the breadth of his interests and his lifelong commitment to storytelling.

	He was also an accomplished photographer and writer. He published a novel, “Of Love and Evil: The Birth,” a gothic story weaving history, love, mystery and the supernatural.

	Hubert’s family describes him as a storyteller at heart. “Whether working with moving images in an editing room, directing actors, developing a screenplay, looking through the lens of his camera or putting words onto a page, he was drawn throughout his life to creativity and artistic expression,” the family wrote in a statement.
	

	De la Bouillerie is survived by his two children, Jacqueline Bell and Alexandre de la Bouillerie, as well as his sister Annie Goeke and his siblings Caroline Gruber, Juliette Glazebrook, Diane Cottrell, Helie de la Bouillerie and Alban de la Bouillerie.

schema.headline: Hubert de la Bouillerie, Editor on ‘Woodstock,’ ‘Witches of Eastwick,’ Dies at 75

title: Neil Young Files $10 Million Suit Against Trump for Using ‘Rockin’ in the Free World,’ Six Years After a Prior Settlement Over the Same Song
description: Neil Young has filed a $10 million lawsuit Monday against Donald J. Trump‘s political action committee, Trump 47 Committee Inc., alleging copyright
body:
Neil Young has filed a $10 million lawsuit Monday against Donald J. Trump‘s political action committee, Trump 47 Committee Inc., alleging copyright infringement for the ongoing use of Young’s song “Rockin’ in the Free World” as the president’s walkup music at midterm election rallies.

	If it feels like (to quote a Crosby, Stills, Nash & Young song) “we have all been here before,” the deja vu comes from the fact that this is Young’s second time filing suit against Trump over his unlicensed appropriation of “Rockin’ in the Free World.” The first was in 2020, and that lawsuit was settled, only for Trump to continue to play it again now, against the terms of the prior settlement, according to Young’s suit.
	

	The suit says the classic 1989 song is “a blistering anthem that contrasts the hollow promises of American political rhetoric with the harsh realities faced by the poor, homeless and forgotten. The lyrics pain vivid street-level portraits — a mother discarding her baby, addicts lost in despair, garbage piling in the shadows of prosperity — while the repeated chorus delivers a savage irony, celebrating freedom that clearly isn’t shared by all. In short, the song is the opposite of everything that Donald J. Trump stands for.”

	Variety has reviewed the suit, which was filed by Young against the Trump 47 Committee Monday in the U.S. district court for the eastern district of Virginia. It specifically cites the playing of the song at the president’s rally in Youngstown, Ohio on Oct. 12, although it notes that the recording has also been played “numerous times at other rallies designed to encourage Republican votes in the upcoming mid-term elections.” It asks for an injunction against further public performance for political purposes as well as the $10 million in damages for the existing use.
	

	It says that Trump “is now and at the time of all rallies this year was personally aware that a license would be required to play the song at rallies and that Young has not, and would not, grant the required license.” The suit then goes on to state that in 2020 Young sued a different corporation formed by the president, Donald J. Trump for President Inc,, for copyright infringement of “Rock'” plus another song of Young’s.

	“Donald J. Trump for President Inct. asserted no defense and immediate;y settled shortly after it was served, promising that it would never again use ‘Rockin’ in the Free World’ without a license and permission from Young.” This new lawsuit does not specify any financial or other terms of the 2020 settlement.

	“Among other things, Young has suffered damage to his reputation and brand as a result of the implication that he supports Donald J. Trump in any way,” the suit contends.

	Young has been among the most vocal of all musicians going public with vociferous opposition to Trump, making it difficult to know whether the president’s ongoing use of Young’s most famously anti-Republican song is being done out of ignorance or as a deliberate finger in the rocker’s face.

	Of course, the White House has often deliberately trolled pop stars this year by using their songs in videos promoting ICE or the war in Iran, then mocking the musicians when they speak up on social media.

	The current leading headline on Young’s Archives website is “The Tragic Death of the Republican Party,” over a reprinted column by writer Robert Reich. The musician’s site is filled with similar signed and unsigned columns, some written by Young himself. An unsigned editorial posted on his front page Oct. 1 begins, “Trump by any standards has been the most corrupt president in the history of the United States. What’s remarkable is that it’s done with little effort to hide it. It’s this corruption that appears to finally be motivating his supporters to turn against him.”

schema.headline: Neil Young Files $10 Million Suit Against Trump for Using ‘Rockin’ in the Free World,’ Six Years After a Prior Settlement Over the Same Song

title: Searchlight Pictures Marketing EVP Michelle Hooper Exits Studio
description:
Michelle Hooper is leaving Searchlight Pictures as executive vice president of marketing after two decades with the company.

	Since joining in 200
body:
Michelle Hooper is leaving Searchlight Pictures as executive vice president of marketing after two decades with the company.

	Since joining in 2006, Hooper’s work on publicity, awards and creative marketing helped earn the studio nearly 200 Oscar nominations and more than 130 Golden Globe nominations. Of those 200, Searchlight took home 49 wins, including best picture winners “Nomadland,” “The Shape of Water,” “Birdman,” “12 Years a Slave” and “Slumdog Millionaire.” Searchlight also received best picture nominations at the Golden Globes for the aforementioned titles, in addition to 15 others.
	

	This awards season, Hooper was leading campaigns for “Wild Horse Nine” and “Behemonth!,” among other titles.

	“She’s a stellar leader for her creative insights and keen ability to read a film for where it fits in the zeitgeist, in turn setting her team up for wide-reaching success,” said a longtime colleague. “But she’s also an equally formidable collaborator, one who can close a campaign with all the insights gained from keeping her ear to the ground and hearing feedback in real time. It’s a loss for the studio, but I guarantee you it will be another’s gain.”

	Earlier in her career, Hooper worked at CBS Entertainment as the director of entertainment communications and aided in the “Survivor” publicity strategy; she also spent four years at Fox Broadcast as the company’s VP of entertainment publicity, where she worked on campaigns for shows like “The Simpsons,” “Arrested Development” and “American Idol.”
	

	Hooper was featured in Variety’s 2025 Women’s Impact Report alongside fellow Searchlight executives Rebecca Kearey, DanTram Nguyen and Katie Goodson-Thomas, whose work to ensure the studio had a stellar year at the Oscars was highlighted.

	“The team’s marketing mojo led to 10 Academy Award nominations for ‘A Complete Unknown’ and ‘A Real Pain,’ including a best supporting actor win for Kieran Culkin’s performance in the Jesse Eisenberg film,” wrote Variety.

	In a joint statement, the team explained that Searchlight’s adventurous choices and deep filmmaker relationships help the company weather the challenges of the business by “trusting [that] audiences still want films that entertain, challenge and provoke.”

schema.headline: Searchlight Pictures Marketing EVP Michelle Hooper Exits Studio

title: ‘Nobody Wants This’ Star Tovah Feldshuh Responds to Adam Brody’s Palestine Support: ‘To Accuse the Jewish People of Genocide’ Is ‘Right Out of Hitler’s Playbook’
description:
“Nobody Wants This” star Tovah Feldshuh has weighed in after Adam Brody called for a “Free Palestine” during a GQ interview last month. 

	At the t
body:
“Nobody Wants This” star Tovah Feldshuh has weighed in after Adam Brody called for a “Free Palestine” during a GQ interview last month. 

	At the time, the actor, who plays Rabbi Noah Roklov on the Netflix show, explained that while he hadn’t spoken publicly about the Israel-Gaza issue before, it comes up “a lot” for him in private. He then made his stance on the conflict clear: “Put me down as thinking it’s a genocide,” he said. “Put me down as wanting a free Palestine. It’s awful that it’s taken so much death and misery, but it does feel like it’s reaching a breaking point that it should have a while ago.”
	

	On Sunday, speaking about Brody, Feldshuh told The New York Post that “to accuse the Jewish people of genocide is wild. It’s right out of Hitler’s playbook. You take the victim, and you make the victim the perpetrator.” When these accusations come from Jewish people themselves, it “makes a difference to the [Jewish] community,” she added. 

	She continued: “I believe that the perseverance of the existence of the state of Israel is crucial to the well-being of the democratic world and of the free world… Of course, Israel needs the United States, [but] the United States needs Israel, believe me.” “We’re in a time where we have the ‘horseshoe effect,’ where socialism and antisemitism are trying to meet,” she said.

	Feldshuh plays Bina Roklov in “Nobody Wants This,” the mother of Brody’s character. “My job, as Bina but also as Tovah, is to love the people on set at my place of work, to be kind,” she said.
	

	Earlier this month, “Nobody Wants This” creator Erin Foster responded to Brody’s support for Palestine, saying: “I disagree with him, and that’s OK.”

	“You know, it’s complicated,” Foster said of Brody’s comments while a guest on the “Not Skinny but Not Fat” podcast. “I think our work environment, our set is very similar to dinner tables around the world where people are having debate and discussion and disagreeing. And, you know, while I love Adam, I also disagree with him, and that’s OK.”

schema.headline: ‘Nobody Wants This’ Star Tovah Feldshuh Responds to Adam Brody’s Palestine Support: ‘To Accuse the Jewish People of Genocide’ Is ‘Right Out of Hitler’s Playbook’

title: Jay-Z to Perform at Apple Music 2027 Super Bowl Halftime Show
description: Jay-Z is slated to perform at the Apple Music Super Bowl LXI Halftime Show, taking place on Feb. 14, 2027, at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, California
body:
Jay-Z is slated to perform at the Apple Music Super Bowl LXI Halftime Show, taking place on Feb. 14, 2027, at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, California.

	“From Reasonable Doubt to standing on the Super Bowl Halftime stage, this has been a journey,” said Jay-Z in a statement. “Thirty years of music, work, and culture on the world’s biggest stage. This run continues to be a dream come true.”


	The announcement comes on the heels of an anniversary victory lap this year under the banner “Jay-Z 30.” He kicked off the celebrations as a headliner at the Roots Picnic in late May, followed by three sold-out shows at Yankee Stadium in July to honor the 25th and 30th anniversaries of his albums “The Blueprint” and “Reasonable Doubt,” respectively. In addition to international shows in Paris and London, Jay sat down with Rick Rubin for the eight-part docuseries “Jay-Z in 8” where he broke down hits and deep cuts across his catalog. This past weekend, he brought his global string of tour dates to a close at SoFi Stadium with two nights featuring guest appearances from Scarface, DJ Khaled, John Legend, Blue Ivy Carter, Dr. Dre, Snoop Dogg and Too Short.
	



	“For several years, we’ve had the privilege of working closely with Jay-Z and Roc Nation, and I’ve seen the extraordinary impact he has had on the Super Bowl Halftime Show,” said NFL Commissioner Roger Goodell in a statement. “When we first reached an agreement with Roc Nation to produce the show, I had just one request: that Jay-Z take the stage himself one day, whenever the moment felt right to him. I couldn’t be more excited for fans around the world to experience the artistry, creativity and cultural impact he will bring to the Super Bowl stage.”
	

	“Jay-Z’s impact on global music culture is as profound as it is undeniable,” added Oliver Schusser, Apple’s Vice President of Music and International Content. “We’ve had the privilege of working closely with him these last few years to bring some of the world’s most exciting and prolific artists to the Super Bowl Halftime Show stage and we are so thrilled that he will be taking that stage himself this year. We know it’s going to be an incredible show.”

	The Super Bowl Halftime Show will air on ESPN, ABC and Disney+, and on mobile devices with NFL+. ESPN’s Spanish-language telecast will also be available on ESPN Deportes and Disney+, with a separate Spanish-language presentation on Univision. Roc Nation will executive produce the show, while Hamish Hamilton will serve as director.



	

	



	Earlier this year, Bad Bunny held court as the Super Bowl Halftime Show performer, celebrating his Puerto Rican heritage in the tradition of Latin America. The elaborate set included a mock sugar-cane field and a Puerto Rican vecindad with a barber shop, liquor store and a casita where Bad Bunny welcomed celebrity guests including Jessica Alba, Karol G, Cardi B, Young Miko and Pedro Pascal, among others. Bad Bunny also brought out surprise artists Lady Gaga and Ricky Martin for a salsa-inflected version of “Die With a Smile” and “lo que le pasó a Hawái,” respectively.

	The Benito Bowl, as it was affectionately dubbed by his fans, reached an average of 128.2 million viewers, above the 124.9 million average viewers achieved by the Super Bowl overall but down from the 133.5 million viewers reached by Kendrick Lamar in 2025. Before Lamar, Usher held the record for most viewers with his 2024 performance.

	Last month, Bad Bunny won his first Emmy for his Super Bowl Halftime Show performance in the outstanding special (live) category. The spectacle took home a total of seven wins, including musical direction, choreography, sound mixing, lighting design, technical direction/camerawork and directing.

	Speaking about the performance, creative director Harriet Cuddeford previously told Variety, “The performance is celebrating normal people, and what it is to be human and love and have joy, and really appreciate one another. This was to show how much he values his community, to celebrate normal people on the world’s biggest stage, especially people who are of importance in Latino culture. He’s a very authentic person, Benito, and it’s about just being authentic and very real and very human.”
	

	In addition to the aforementioned artists, recent performers at the Super Bowl Halftime Show have included Rihanna, the Weeknd and a collective performance from Dr. Dre, Snoop Dogg, Eminem, Mary J. Blige, Lamar, 50 Cent and Anderson .Paak.

schema.headline: Jay-Z to Perform at Apple Music 2027 Super Bowl Halftime Show

title: Macklemore Calls for Unity During First ‘Free Palestine’ Show as Hozier, Kneecap and Mark Ruffalo Support: ‘Those Two Words Are So Threatening to Some People’
description: Macklemore dedicated his first “Free Palestine” tour date in Dublin, Ireland to “love and liberation,” just over a month after he was dropped as an
body:
Macklemore dedicated his first “Free Palestine” tour date in Dublin, Ireland to “love and liberation,” just over a month after he was dropped as an opener for Ed Sheeran following a political speech on stage.

	3Arena was dotted with keffiyehs and Palestinian flags on Monday night as Dubliners young and old gathered to back the “Thrift Shop” rapper at the start of the three-show stint, which will also see him play Paris and London this week alongside special guests. All proceeds are going to charities supporting Palestine, and Macklemore also donated his $1 million salary from Sheeran’s tour to the cause.
	

	To recap, on Sept. 14 Macklemore was dropped from the remainder of Sheeran’s U.S. “Loop” tour after he said “free Palestine” on stage and gave political speeches over two concerts at New Jersey’s MetLife Stadium on Sept. 4 and 5. The speeches went viral, sparking backlash from pop star Pink and a petition from the Israeli American Council calling for his removal and criticizing him for using the platform to “advance a political agenda.” At the time, promoter Messina Touring Group said they had been “notified by venues” that “they will not allow a concert to take place with Macklemore on the lineup.” Macklemore claimed that it was Gillette Stadium owner Robert Kraft who had pushed him out of the tour, and Sheeran also posted a lengthy statement explaining why he doesn’t wade into politics, which generated backlash against him. In solidarity with Macklemore, Sheeran’s other opening acts — including Finneas, Lukas Graham and Aaron Rowe — and his backing band, Beoga, also dropped out of his tour.
	

	Beoga was there to support Macklemore on Monday, alongside surprise guests including Hozier and Kneecap. During his set, Macklemore took a moment to share what the evening meant to him in the wake of the controversy. “Six weeks ago, it was two words. Two words is all that it took. Two words that are rooted in love and liberation,” he said. “Not against anybody, not divisive. Not a call for hatred. But a call to recognize our shared humanity. Free Palestine. I said, free Palestine! The same thing that I want for all of us, freedom, dignity, the right to exist without fear. Being able to raise our children in the homes that we grew up in, not having to prove our humanity to the rest of the world.

	“And yet,” he continued, “those two words are so threatening to some people. They would rather silence those two words than confront what they actually mean. Because freedom that requires another person’s oppression is not freedom at all. And while the world debates those words, we see the videos, we see the footage, we see parents pulling their children out of the rubble. Families erased. Devastation beyond our imagination. And somehow, those words have become more controversial than the suffering that made them necessary. That’s why we are here tonight. That is why we are here, because throughout history, music has given people a place to resist, to come together as a collective, to share our grief, to share our stories, to move from the heart, to mobilize people with the frequency of love. The heartbeat in our drum that makes us feel alive, that makes us feel connected.”


	But before Macklemore took the stage, the night kicked off with an introduction from Liam Cunningham of “Game of Thrones” fame. “Tonight, we celebrate life. We honor resilience. We stand with Gaza!” he said. The music then began with Palestinian-Israeli singer Lina Makoul, who delivered a powerful song without words “because anything she said could have severely affected her freedom,” as Cunningham noted. Beoga was next, performing several traditional Irish jigs after percussionist Eamon Murray told the crowd, “Don’t fuck with the Irish!”

	The first heavyweight guest was none other than Hozier, who got the crowd crooning along with “Too Sweet,” “From Eden,” and “Work Song.” The Irishman said he is “so proud of my country and the way they’re showing up,” and highlighted that 55 students in Gaza are waiting to have their visas approved by the Irish government so that they can study there. “This has happened before. It happened last year, and this can be solved with ministerial discretion,” he continued. “It’s an absolute wonder, it’s baffling how it hasn’t been solved yet.”
	

	Seeming uncharacteristically nervous, Hozier then announced that he was going to perform a tune that he’d “never sang live before.” It was “The Prayer of Shields,” an 18th-century folk song written by John Shield that hoped for equality for all people. “The Jew he is me fellow man/ The Muslim the same indeed, sir,” he sang in a haunting tone. “To the infidel I’d wish him well/And help him in his need, sir.”

	As the stage was reset, the crowd was treated to a series of video messages from celebrities who couldn’t be there but wanted to show their support. “Thanks to Macklemore for doing this,” The Strokes frontman Julian Casablancas said. “Take care of each other and the innocents, and continue standing up in this struggle towards a just world system.”

	Added “Broad City” star Ilana Glazer, “We are all together in this fight to help free Palestine. Keep speaking up and using your voice, it’s working.”

	“Keep fighting for a free Palestine and humanity all over the world and amongst the people. There will be no peace until there’s equality,” Mark Ruffalo said to enthusiastic applause throughout the stadium. “Lots of love, have a good show. Keep fighting the good fight.”


	Irish rap trio Kneecap then stormed the arena, injecting a dose of energy by getting mosh pits going in the crowd as they ran through fan favorites like “Fenian” and “H.O.O.D.” “We wanna thank Macklemore for organizing this concert. We wanna thank Ed Sheeran for helping to organize this concert,” member Móglaí Bap cheekily said as the crowd erupted in cheers.

	It was then finally time for Macklemore’s set. The rapper was greeted with enormous applause as he emerged in a green-and-orange keffiyeh to “Chant,” with Australian singer Tones and I joining him to sing the chorus. Supported by a six-piece band, Macklemore rapped with conviction: “This is my moment/ They can’t take my talent/ They can’t take my stripes.” He addressed the crowd for the first time as the song finished, looking overwhelmed and wiping tears from his eyes. Before he could begin to speak, a “free Palestine” chant broke out in the audience. 

	“It has been a crazy six weeks,” he said. “We took my shortest tour of all time, which was two nights at MetLife Stadium, and we turned that shit into this right here.” He added, “We’re gonna start with an anti-capitalist anthem,” as his hit “Thrift Shop” rang out and a pair of peppy dancers two-stepped on stage.
	

	A run-down of Macklemore’s greatest hits ensued, including “Same Love” with Mary Lambert joining him; “These Days”; “Glorious”; and “Good Old Days,” with Tones and I reemerging to sing Kesha’s part on the track. He then surprised the audience with a new song that “he wrote this last week,” titled “Where Is Our Love?” In the political yet soft-spoken rap, Macklemore says “free Palestine” and speaks about “America being terrorized by ICE agents” as well as mentioning Congo and Sudan. 

	The set ended on a high note with his 2012 hit “Can’t Hold Us,” during which Macklemore climbed into the crowd and had them literally hold him up. As confetti exploded in the air, Macklemore left the audience with one last message: “I am proud to stand here on stage in solidarity with the Palestinian people. We will continue to fight for collective liberation until our last breath,” he said before leading one final “free Palestine” chant.

	Macklemore’s “Free Palestine” tour continues in Paris on Thursday and London on Friday.

schema.headline: Macklemore Calls for Unity During First ‘Free Palestine’ Show as Hozier, Kneecap and Mark Ruffalo Support: ‘Those Two Words Are So Threatening to Some People’

title: ‘The Odyssey’ VFX House DNEG Co-Finances Francesco Lucente’s Fantasy Adventure ‘Sinbad,’ Cappu Films Boards Sales (EXCLUSIVE)
description: DNEG, the visual effects house on Christopher Nolan’s “The Odyssey,” has come aboard Francesco Lucente’s fantasy adventure “Sinbad” as co-financier
body:
DNEG, the visual effects house on Christopher Nolan’s “The Odyssey,” has come aboard Francesco Lucente’s fantasy adventure “Sinbad” as co-financier and producer, with Hong Kong-based Cappu Films handling sales in a wide spread of territories.

	The deal was unveiled ahead of the Tokyo International Film Festival‘s TIFFCOM market. Lucente’s fresh screen version of the classic sailor tale is due to begin pre-production in early 2027 and to deliver in March 2029. 
	

	Cappu first showed the project to buyers at the Busan market, and sales conversations are ongoing as casting and the wider package take shape.

	“‘Sinbad’ is a story that has captured imaginations for generations, and our ambition is to bring it to life on a scale and with a sense of wonder that audiences have never experienced before,” said Lucente, who wrote the script and will direct. “We’re creating a breathtaking world of adventure, extraordinary creatures, ancient mysteries and unforgettable characters, while keeping the heart of the story deeply human. Having DNEG’s extraordinary creative talent behind us, together with Cappu Films’ international reach and commitment to the project, gives us an incredible foundation to realize that vision. We want ‘Sinbad’ to be more than a spectacular cinematic experience – we want it to be the kind of adventure that stays with audiences long after they leave the theater.”

	The sales company’s rights cover parts of Asia, Europe, the CIS, Latin America, the Caribbean, the Middle East and Africa, along with some Pacific island markets. China, Hong Kong, Japan, South Korea, German-speaking Europe, Spain, Portugal, Turkey and Eastern Europe are all on the list.
	

	The film reunites Cappu with Lucente after “Starbright.” Janice Woo of Cappu Films said that following their work together on that film, the company was excited to team with the director on a project of this scale. “DNEG’s involvement is particularly compelling for a fantasy adventure such as ‘Sinbad.’ We introduced the project to buyers in Busan and look forward to developing those conversations as the package comes together,” Woo said.

	DNEG’s teams have won eight Oscars for visual effects, and the company’s credits include “Inception,” “Interstellar,” “Blade Runner 2049,” “Dune” and “Dune: Part Two.”

	Lucente’s fantasy feature “Starbright” counts Ted Levine, John Rhys-Davies and Diego Boneta among its cast. He also directed the drama “Badland.” Cappu is separately handling international sales on “A Grim Life,” a supernatural thriller starring Joseph Mazzello and set at Los Angeles’ Cecil Hotel.

	Cappu partners with independent filmmakers on both arthouse and commercial titles. Its catalog takes in horror, action, fantasy and arthouse fare, alongside library titles from Hong Kong’s Golden Era and TV series.

schema.headline: ‘The Odyssey’ VFX House DNEG Co-Finances Francesco Lucente’s Fantasy Adventure ‘Sinbad,’ Cappu Films Boards Sales (EXCLUSIVE)

title: Camille Grammer Blasts Ex Kelsey Grammer for Allegedly Forgetting Daughter's Birthday
description:

                          Kelsey Didn't Even Call Our Daughter on Her 25th Birthd
body:
Camille Grammer
                          Kelsey Didn't Even Call Our Daughter on Her 25th Birthday!!!
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              October 26, 2026
                            5:20 PM PDT
                                                                            
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Camille Grammer is putting her ex-husband Kelsey Grammer on blast ... accusing the "Frasier" star of failing to acknowledge their daughter Mason Grammer's 25th birthday.
      
    
            The 'Real Housewives of Beverly Hills' alum took to Instagram Monday with a scathing message directed at Kelsey ... claiming their daughter hadn't received so much as a phone call or text from her famous father three days after her milestone birthday.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            "A daughter should never have to wonder whether her father remembers her birthday," Camille wrote. "Three days later, and still not a call or a text. 💔"
      

            Camille didn't mention Kelsey by name, but made it pretty clear who she was talking about ... taking aim at a father whose Hollywood success apparently hasn't translated into showing up for his daughter.
      
    
            "You can be a beloved actor to the world, but being a father is a role that requires showing up when the cameras are off," she continued.
      
    
            Camille added that fame, accolades and public admiration mean little when someone neglects the people who should matter most.
      
    
            She wrapped up her post by saying "A mother never stops hurting when her child is hurt. 25 is a milestone birthday. Sometimes the silence is deafening, and the disappointment speaks volumes."
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Camille and Kelsey were married for 13 years before their highly publicized split in 2010. They also share a son, Jude.
      
    
            Their relationship has remained strained over the years, with Camille revealing in May that she and Kelsey hadn't spoken in 14 years.
      
    
            We've reached out to Kelsey's rep for comment.
